description: The portfolio's shared configuration, extended by name: the Monday batch, the limits, the labels, the kotlin/kotlinx/sborka groups, `ci actions` and majors going to a human.

Automerge is a separate preset (`github>youndie/sborka:automerge-harness`) and is not extended: nothing merges itself here today. Its precondition holds — check.yaml runs on `pull_request` — so it can be added as its own change.

packageRules.description: kompot moves as one thing across all three pins, because they are one version wearing three hats: the server compiles against it, the client's types are generated from it, and the corpus is fetched from it. A pull request that moves one of them is a repository that no longer agrees with itself. Named down to `kompot-` rather than the whole `io.github.youndie` group: the portfolio is migrating into that group, and a pattern ending at the group would pull sborka into this rule and label its bumps `kompot`.
prBodyNotes: **This one is not a merge button.** A kompot bump has twice brought protocol changes with it: new fields in the generated types, and new cases in the conformance corpus that the form engine had to be written against. `pnpm schema:check` and `pnpm corpus:check` compare the committed copies against the pinned version, so this will fail until they are regenerated — which is the check doing its job, not the bot being wrong.

After merging the version bump: `pnpm --filter kompot-web schema` and `pnpm --filter kompot-web corpus`, then read the diff. The schema diff answers "what else changed" cheaply; new corpus cases are work.

packageRules.description: The libraries proba itself is built from. Grouped by ecosystem so a red build points at one of them rather than at a pull request that moved nine. kompot is carved out by the rule above; the sborka plugins are carved out so they keep arriving in the preset's `sborka` group, which is what keeps the settings plugin and the conventions on one number.
